html:
The Nari Nari are an Aboriginal people of the Riverina in New South Wales, around the lower Murrumbidgee River near Balranald and Hay.

Historians believe they formed from the joining of several groups in the area, including people of the Wiradjuri and Wadi Wadi. Their western border was with the Muthi Muthi. The river flats and swamps of the Murrumbidgee gave fish, waterbirds and plant foods.

Squatters brought sheep and cattle down the Murrumbidgee in the late 1830s and 1840s, soon after the explorer Charles Sturt followed the river to the Murray in 1830. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Nari Nari are an Aboriginal people of the Riverina in New South Wales, around the lower Murrumbidgee River near Balranald and Hay.
